items.title: Today's lesson
items.content:
Three glasses left on a table overnight open the lesson: the **mud** in muddy water settles, but the **milk** in milky water does not. Why?

Sugar water and sand water sort mixtures into **homogeneous** and **heterogeneous**. Filtering salt water and chalk water introduces **solutions** and **suspensions**; milk introduces **colloids** and the particle-size scale.

A laser beam shows the **Tyndall effect**, which students then spot in sunbeams, fog and dusty rooms.

Some pictures have a **second picture or animation**: show picture 1, ask, then click ›.

items.title: You already know
items.content:
• a mixture: two or more substances mixed without combining chemically

• solute, solvent and solution (sugar in water)

• filtration and settling (sedimentation)

items.title: By the end, you can
items.content:
**1.** Classify mixtures as homogeneous or heterogeneous.

**2.** Distinguish solutions, colloids and suspensions, including the Tyndall effect.

**3.** Identify everyday examples of each.

items.prompt: Classify, in order: brass, muddy water, soda water, salt mixed with sand. (HO = homogeneous, HE = heterogeneous)
Which of these is a homogeneous mixture?

items.text:
**On this question**

**A**: brass homogeneous; muddy water heterogeneous; soda water homogeneous; salt with sand heterogeneous.

**On this question**

**B**: in vinegar, acetic acid is spread evenly through the water.

items.prompt: A medicine bottle says “Shake well before use”. What type of mixture is it, and why shake it?
options: Colloid: particles stick to the glass

items.text:
**On this question**

**A**: a suspension. Its particles settle at the bottom on standing, so it is shaken to spread them evenly before each dose.

items.prompt: Name the dispersed phase and the dispersion medium in fog and in smoke.
options: Fog: water in air; smoke: solid in air
Fog: air in water; smoke: air in solid
Fog: solid in air; smoke: water in air
Fog: water in air; smoke: air in solid

items.text:
**On this question**

**A**: fog is water droplets (dispersed phase) in air (dispersion medium); smoke is solid particles in air.

items.text:
